company_description: The Travelers Companies, Inc., through its subsidiaries, provides a range of commercial and personal property, and casualty insurance products and services to businesses, government units, associations, and individuals in the United States, Canada, and internationally. It operates through three segments: Business Insurance, Bond & Specialty Insurance, and Personal Insurance. The Business Insurance segment offers workers' compensation, commercial automobile and property, general liability, commercial multi-peril, employers' liability, public and product liability, professional indemnity, marine, aviation, commercial property and automobile, onshore and offshore energy, construction, terrorism, personal accident, and kidnap and ransom insurance products. This segment operates through select accounts, which serve small businesses; middle accounts that serve mid-sized businesses; national accounts, which serve large companies; and national property and others that serve large and mid-sized customers, commercial trucking industry, and agricultural businesses, as well as markets and distributes its products through brokers, wholesale agents, and program managers. kpis.name: Investment Portfolio
kpis.explanation: Fair value of total invested assets including fixed maturities, equities, and other securities.
kpis.description: The investment portfolio is primarily composed of fixed income securities (89% in debt securities) intended to fund claim reserves.

kpis.name: Interest Rate Risk Sensitivity
kpis.explanation: Estimated fair value loss from hypothetical 100 basis point increase in interest rates.
kpis.description: Estimated loss of $3.68 billion if interest rates rise by 100 basis points, based on the model's sensitivity analysis.

kpis.name: Foreign Currency Risk Sensitivity
kpis.explanation: Estimated fair value loss from hypothetical 10% depreciation of foreign currency holdings.
kpis.description: Estimated loss of $373 million if foreign-currency-denominated investments depreciate by 10%, declining due to reduced Canadian dollar exposure.

kpis.name: Personal Insurance Combined Ratio
kpis.explanation: Personal Insurance segment combined ratio measuring underwriting efficiency (claims + expenses / earned premiums).
kpis.description: The Personal Insurance combined ratio improved 4.9 points in 2025 to 89.5%, driven by lower auto claims and the benefit of rate increases. In 2023, the segment was loss-making at 104.8%.

kpis.name: Personal Insurance Segment Net Income
kpis.explanation: After-tax net income of the Personal Insurance segment, reflecting overall personal insurance profitability.
kpis.description: The Personal Insurance segment generated $2.05 billion in net income in 2025, up 64% vs 2024, after a $128 million loss in 2023. The recovery is driven by improving auto underwriting margins and higher investment income.

kpis.name: Bond & Specialty Net Written Premiums
kpis.explanation: Net written premiums of the Bond & Specialty Insurance segment, indicator of surety and liability business volume.
kpis.description: Net written premiums of the Bond & Specialty segment reached $4.26 billion in 2025, up 4% year-over-year, driven by domestic surety (+5%) and international (+15%). Growth has been sustained since 2023.

kpis.name: Personal Insurance Active Policies
kpis.explanation: Number of active domestic policies in the Personal Insurance segment, indicator of customer base and business volume.
kpis.description: Active domestic policies declined to 8.4 million at end-2025 vs 8.8 million at end-2024, reflecting increased underwriting selectivity despite premium hikes. International went from 425,000 to 349,000 policies.

kpis.name: Net Asbestos Reserves
kpis.explanation: Net reserves set aside to cover asbestos-related claims, including case reserves, IBNR and legal defense costs.
kpis.description: Net asbestos reserves stood at $1.36 billion at end-2025, up a modest $20 million vs 2024. This residual liability reflects historical exposure in run-off, with complex litigation and ongoing settlements.

kpis.name: Combined Ratio
kpis.explanation: Measures the ratio of insurance costs to premiums received. Ratio below 100% means profitability.

kpis.name: Net Written Premiums
kpis.explanation: Measures the insurance premiums Travelers collects after deductions, revealing its actual commercial revenue.

kpis.name: Net Investment Income
kpis.explanation: Measures the revenue Travelers generates from its financial investments, a key overall profitability indicator.

kpis.name: Book Value per Share
kpis.explanation: Measures the real value of each share based on net assets, indicating whether the stock is cheap or expensive.

kpis.name: Return on Equity
kpis.explanation: Measures the profit generated with shareholders' money. Indicates the efficiency of financial management.

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.description: Annual dividend per share paid, aggregated from yfinance.dividends over the last 7 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Dividend per share of $1.1 in the latest year.

kpis.name: Capital Returned (Dividends)
kpis.description: Capital returned to shareholders via annual dividends, extracted from yfinance.cashflow over the last 4 reported fiscal years.
kpis.signal: Capital returned to shareholders via dividends of $0.979 billion in the latest year.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.description: Payout Ratio = Dividends Paid / Net Income, calculated over the last 4 fiscal years from yfinance.cashflow and yfinance.income_stmt.
kpis.signal: Share of net income distributed as dividends: 15.6% in the latest year.
